saints.name: St. Gregory the Great
saints.title: Pope and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The Roman prefect turned monk who as pope styled himself "servant of the servants of God" and shepherded the Church through a broken age…
biography: Born about 540 of a Roman senatorial family, Gregory became prefect of the city, then gave his wealth to found monasteries and made his father's palace on the Caelian Hill the monastery of St. Andrew, where he lived as a monk. He served later as deacon and as papal envoy at Constantinople, where he began his Moralia on Job.

In 590, when Pelagius II died of the plague, clergy and people chose him pope, and he was consecrated on 3 September. He fed the starving city from the Church's estates, made treaties with the Lombards, and in 596 sent Augustine and his monks to convert the English.

His Pastoral Rule formed bishops for centuries, his Dialogues preserved the memory of St. Benedict, and the chant of the Roman Church bears his name. When the Patriarch of Constantinople claimed the title ecumenical, he answered by taking the style 'servant of the servants of God,' which the popes bear still.

Worn out by gout and labor, he died on 12 March 604 and was buried in St. Peter's. One of the four great Latin Doctors, he is patron of musicians for his chant and of teachers for his school of pastoral writings.
saints.knownFor: The mission to the English and his reform of the Church's liturgy and pastoral life.

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; Doctor of the Church
